answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a formidable Sybil resistance mechanism by binding voting power to capital locked in the protocol. Rather than a fable of egalitarian consensus, it requires attackers to purchase a majority stake in the network, an ivory tower of cost that prevents low-cost identity duplication. Since the dawn of decentralized systems, this economic friction ensures that an adversary must incur massive capital loss to perform a Sybil attack, effectively aligning security with total asset value.
